summary: mgm controller described operational error when realizing ifr traffic that had been handed off was about to enter mva below required altitude; coordination was too late to secure needed separation.
a11 tracon controller reported air carrier on knik2 sid entered higher mva resulting in low altitude alert.
crj200 flt crew has a close encounter with a vehicle while taxiing at ord.

a maintenance golf car struck a b737-800 engine inlet after the mechanic dropped his cordless drill on the seat; it then bounced off only to be wedged on the gas pedal which started the engine and released the brake.
a319 flight crew reported the aircraft rolled backwards uncommanded when ground personnel removed chocks prior to brakes set. flight crew applied brakes to stop aircraft.
a b757-200 captain discovered that his aircraft's non-pegasus fmc did not have certain european airport in its database which were listed as enroute etops alternates.
regional jet first officer reported receiving a gpws terrain warning; while performing a 360 to lose altitude; on a night visual approach to eug.
a320 flt crew refuses to accept the acft for flt until conformity and integrity tests are performed.
c182 plt lndg rwy 3 at mkc exits onto rwy 1 which is notamed closed for tkof and lndgs. tower advises not to exit on rwy 1 unless cleared to do so.

air carrier captain reported a communications breakdown between flight crew and ground personnel; resulting in flight crew being provided with erroneous hazmat documents. multiple handling errors also resulted in dangerous goods and a kidney not loaded on aircraft.

pilot reports of flying into sdm and not being familiar with the jump zones that are close to the airport. controller vectors aircraft for a visual approach; leaves the aircraft high; and then ships the aircraft to the tower. aircraft turns away from airport to continue its descent and tower controller advises pilot he is going into a jump zone. pilot finally lands at sdm. pilot reports that this is an unsafe operation and offers suggestions to make flying into sdm better.
c206 pilot turns onto rwy 19l from txwy b when intending to turn onto txwy a at ccr; citing lack of signage.

air carrier ramp personnel reported refusing supervisor's order to clean up liquid on class 9 hazmat package. ramp agent's refusal was based on company hazmat cleanup policy which requires specific training to do so.
air carrier flight crew reported a nmac with a helicopter shortly after takeoff from isp airport.
crj-900 first officer reported that miscommunication with atc resulted in evasive action to avoid another aircraft.

a small aircraft pilot flying over a dry lake bed near 0l7 (jean; nv) struck a parasail related cable attached to a wench but the area is not marked on the sectional as supporting recreational aviation activities.
b737-700 captain reported severe turbulence and wind shear conditions necessitating a diversion to an airport with more favorable weather conditions.

while practicing landings in a cirrus sr20 in preparation for a single engine rating; this 300 hour multi-engine and instrument rated pilot lost control of the aircraft during touchdown; exited the runway; and made contact with at least one runway light; causing a small dent in a wing flap.
zmp controller voiced concerns regarding the functionality of eram equipment.

sdl local controller reports of a attempted handoff late from p50. sdl controller advises he's unable handoff due to other traffic. minutes later the aircraft is on his frequency cleared for a visual approach. sdl controller had to send an aircraft around due to the overtake from the un-handed off aircraft. a new loa went into place 3 days prior.
a319 captain reported being unable to accomplish a proper preflight inspection with the towbar-less tractor in place at the gate.

erj 170/175 flight attendant reported an injury caused by the main cabin door liner not positioned correctly; causing her hand to be pinched between the door operating handle and the liner. this resulted in an aircraft change.

air carrier captain reported being notified by atc of going off course. the flight crew was flying towards the wrong fix; radds; and should have been flying direct to rapzz. the two fixes were similar in name and on the same route.
helicopter pilot reported that he flew over another helicopter that was air taxiing after a parallel approach; but was on another frequency.
a ce750 flt crew was cleared for the rnav rwy 26 approach to fxe from the northeast. they flew to the iaf (forsu) and executed a procedure turn; which was not expected by the controller.
pa28 plt has a fuel starvation enrte to dest.
md-80 flight crew reported returning to departure airport after the aft flight attendant called to report a strong burning odor in the aft galley.
b737 crossed rwy hold line at boi while taxiing to assigned rwy as ga acft landed.
be99 executed a gar when midfield tfc announced; 'go around!'
air taxi flight crew reported during landing the aircraft landed with the pilot flying applying the brakes resulting in the nose wheel coming down hard on the runway.
abnormal nose gear retraction results in return to dep arpt for md88.

a controller reported shipping an aircraft to the tower assuming it would turn from downwind onto base leg in time to be in front of straight in traffic. the downwind aircraft turned base late and into conflict with the straight in traffic.
confused by the existence of both a filed rte they shouldn't fly and cleared rte they should have on their acars delivered pdc; mlg flt crew picks the wrong one and has a track dev.
b757 captain reported fatigue on an oceanic crossing with a 2 man crew.
captain reported receiving different altitude assignments from atc after a frequency change.
a tracon controller reported an aircraft on approach descended below their assigned altitude and flew below the minimum vectoring altitude.
plt of vintage pt19 trainer loses ctl during taxi and strikes beechcraft.
an acr dispatch reports losing operational control of numerous short flts in the sector because of overloads due to wx and mechanicals.
md88 flt crew has a track hdg dev during holding clrnc.
b737 flight crew reported during climb they got a number two engine overheat indications. all engine parameters were normal and no visual evidence of problems with the #2 engine was observed.
a c525's left tire failed on landing causing the aircraft to veer uncontrollably left off the runway.
c182 plts activated the elt during flt. the acft was then believed to be missing; and the cap was alerted.

during return to base in a bell bht-222 helicopter; a medic informs pilot there was 'fog' in the cabin and a strong smell of jet fuel after the environmental control system (ecs) was turned on. pilot found oil leaking from bolts on #2 engine compressor case.
a local controller reports that flight crews regularly utilize the incorrect frequency to contact the tower despite frequency publication on the atis.
maintenance technician reported that fumes in the cabin has become a difficult issue to resolve.

an a320 ecam alerted auto brks and norm brks when the gear was extended for landing but no corresponding norm brks checklist was found so during the go around the crew cycled the antiskid switch as per the auto brks ecam which switched to the alternate bscu and removed the ecam alerts. during this event the cockpit was illuminated by a green laser which appeared to have a lock on and which caused eye discomfort.

c162 pilot reports a runway excursion during a gusty crosswind landing that ends in a go around after contacting a runway light. incident is attributed to lack of recent experience in this aircraft at very light weight with gusty crosswinds. also cited was the strange motion of the c162 'stoke.'
pilot reported taking evasive action on the take-off roll when they encountered a motorcycle on the runway.
a c560 in mountainous terrain stepped down to an apch fix early activating gpws terrain warning. the pilot confused the mfd way pt with the chart fix.
pilot reported that they crossed a hwd airport taxiway hold-short line in an area that is known for this recurring problem due to taxiway non-standard location.

crj 900 first officer reported an engine temperature exceedance at cruise and then during descent a bleed warning malfunction resulting in a cabin depressurization. the flight diverted to an alternate airport and landed safely.
dispatcher reported they were task saturated and their desk has a heavy workload. dispatcher expressed concern that 5g-related notams and additional flights increase the workload.
b737-200 left main gear would not retract. uneventful precautionary lndg performed at dest arpt.

a pilot departing o61 non-towered airport reported they observed an arriving aircraft head on to them as they were taking off and had to turn to avoid them. the reporter thought they heard the aircraft report inbound to the opposite direction runway they departed from.

dispatched to ito; aware the last 1;750 feet of runway 26 was closed the captain of an overwater b737ng refused to continue to destination when advised by dispatch while enroute that the first 2;000 feet of the runway edge lights on the runway were also out of service.  the reporter rejected strong advocacy from the dispatcher that the operation was legal.
an md80 prior to dep was found with a nose lndg gear running hyd leak. technician disconnected leaking fitting; reconnected and tightened. leak chk ok.
air carrier first officer reported the sbgr ils rwy 09r approach chart is inaccurate and confusing.

a cessna 421 pilot lost power in the right engine shortly after reaching cruise altitude of fl230.  diverted to a nearby airport even though the engine regained power during the descent to a useable single engine altitude.
fll tower controller reported a runway incursion caused by a vehicle entering the runway while an air carrier was flaring to land.

c182 pilot learns how long his aircraft will fly starting with full tanks and one fuel cap not installed (two hours). a successful engine off landing is accomplished at the nearest airport and the problem is diagnosed.
b767-300 captain reported being on short final at 300 ft agl and having to execute a go-around after atc cleared an aircraft for takeoff; but did not depart in time.
a319 instructor is fatigued and unable to accept another assignment.

b767-300 flight crew experiences a le flap asym during approach when flaps are selected to one. the qrh is consulted resulting in landing with te flaps 20 and vref 30 + 30 (168 kias). the aircraft had a long history of similar problems.
air carrier captain reported an inability to communicate with mem center on arrival into gtr.

lr45 captain experienced a failure of the landing gear to retract after takeoff along with a nose wheel steering fail message and elects to divert to a more suitable airport. after landing it is discovered that the nose gear strut has collapsed.

a tower controller and the two b737 pilots involved describe a takeoff without clearance from pdx. the b737 crew took the clearance for another flight and failed to respond when the tower attempted to stop them.

emb190 flight crew describes a miscommunication during approach during which the captain states 'we may have to go around; flaps 5' (full). the first officer hears go around; flaps 2 and selects 2 then asks about the gear. at this point the captain conveys that he intends to land; flaps 5 is selected and the unstable approach is continued to landing.
b787 flight crew reported fuel concern enroute to yssy was exacerbated when atc required a declaration of minimum fuel in order to avoid a delay.
an instructor administering a pilot's standardization check at 2;500 ft reported a near miss after a small jet passed overhead while it was under mco tracon radar vectors for sfb practice approaches.
air carrier flight attendant reported being rushed by the gate agent and not being informed about air marshals and an escorted prisoner before boarding.
crj200 flt crew has track/hdg devs during the lga 9 dep.

a b737 flt crew failed to follow mel procedures on takeoff with an eng bleed inop and the aircraft would not pressurize. when normal pressurization could not be restored with the procedure; the flt crew diverted to nearest suitable arpt.
atct lcl ctlr rpts a320 executes gar on short final due to unauth vehicle tfc on rwy.
pilot reported the approach lacks glidepath guidance and currently the papi system is notam'd out of service until august.
b777 capt reports reroute in foreign airspace to comply with notam not supplied by dispatcher. min fuel is declared at destination.
air carrier flight crew reported receiving what was suspected to be an erroneous aural terrain warning while intercepting the runway 17 localizer at mht.
md-10 captain reported a loud bang on takeoff with a red indication for the landing gear and elected to return to the departure airport.
emb-175 captain reported increased stress; confusion and loss of situational awareness; partially due to having an faa inspector onboard; which ultimately led to a go-around.
b737-800 flt crew has flap malfunction on apch to mia.
a c182 plt was clred into pos on the rwy for tkof in conflict with a c172 on short final.
air carrier flight crew reported an over speed during departure and cited lack of flying as a contributing factor.
an acr plt describes a state of fatigue so deep that he did not realize until after rest how fatigued he was the previous day.
cl60 flt crew has no brakes or steering on lndg.
an a320 slat extension sys failed for the second consecutive flt. no slat lndg accomplished.

a line mechanic reports he incorrectly applied an mel maintenance procedure to a deferral of the standby pressure controller transfer lockout light on an md-80. aircraft was unable to pressurize at takeoff requiring an air turnback. mechanic noted the mel maintenance procedure page appeared to apply to mel 21-23a and not just mel 21-23b.

piper j3 cub pilot reported while on short final; another aircraft entered the runway for departure resulting in the pilot taking evasive action to avoid a collision with the departing aircraft.  after landing; the pilot was informed their radio was not transmitting in a readable manner.
md80 captain discoverd 500 ft altimeter error in his altimeter passing fl180. flight remained below rvsm airspace and continued to destination with dispatch's concurance.

b737 flight crew reported the aircraft's flight computer lost its vnav capability. the aircraft was unable to comply with two crossing restrictions until the crew was able to reprogram the fmc and vnav path.

a pilot reported the rut ils/loc z runway 19 faf cekra charted crossing altitude is 3;900 ft on glideslope; but his actual experience on three flights; has been a crossing altitude 4;300 ft on glideslope.
c170 pilot reports inadvertently entering mexican airspace near nyl after his efb fails with no paper charts aboard. nyl tower provides assistance.
air carrier captain reported being unable to obtain ppe (personal protective equipment).
a b737-800 crew requested eng fan de-ice prior to eng start. after eng start; crew returned for another eng fan de-ice because of fan vibration.
emb145 flt crew has failure of the #2 bleed air source. during apch in icing conditions; eicas warning 'wing anti-ice fail' illuminates; flt crew clbs above icing conditions and diverts to vfr arpt.
an a300 dispatched with 1 iru mel'ed experience excessive nav sys drift rate resulting in vector nav.
flight instructor reported that while executing the rnav 17 missed approach procedure to uao; atc informed them they had been cleared for a different approach to the same runway.
be35 pilot reported a gear up landing. the gear lever had been selected down; but the gear cb was popped and the gear did not extend.
a c172 instructor plt rpts icing at 6000 ft clbing to 7000 ft. a dscnt to 6000 ft then to 5000 ft clred imc and icing.
b737-700 capt believes company flt fuel planning fails to take potential for foggy conditions at smf into consideration.
falcon 50 fuel feeder tank indicated low fuel. the flt crew was uncertain as to the cause of the anomaly and diverted.
a321 first officer reported windshear escape maneuver resulting in a flap over-speed event.
air carrier flight crew reported receiving non-standard vectors and a gpws terrain warning on an approach to mmmx.
b727 crew cuts corner during turn onto taxiway e from txwy b and gets stuck in the wet grass.
air carrier dispatcher reported frequent task saturation while over seeing flights was further complicated by the presence of volcanic ash in the flights vicinity.
t-6 pilot reported landing gear failed on landing.
an lr40 flight crew returned and landed overweight at its departure airport when the attitude indicator failed immediately after takeoff.
pilot reported z09/pfka airport runway lights were out of service but there was no notam advising pilots of this condition.
an air carrier captain grabbed a toddler who nearly fell through the opening between the rubber jetway bumper and the aircraft door frame because the gap between the two was too wide.

pa-28-180 flight instructor reported a near mid air collision with a helicopter on a converging course immediately after becoming airborne from a tower controlled field.  instructor took controls and made an evasive maneuver to avoid the helicopter.
inexperienced and unfamiliar lj31 flt crew struggle to comply with atc clrncs on vmc arr to lga.
air carrier flight crew exceeded 250 knots below 10;000 feet to expedite to landing airport due to medical emergency of passenger on board.
zob artcc controller reported problems associated with weather and lack of traffic management plans.
an a319 on the clt ivane 2 crossed majic intersection at 12;000 ft because the fmgc dropped the 13;000 ft constraint even though it was verified during the preflight.
b737 first officer reported being sprayed with hydraulic fluid in the eyes while conducting the preflight. they were transported to the hospital for treatment.
a319 captain reported a fumes event during initial approach descent.

flt crew of b747-400 is given fuel boarded form which showed correct total on board; but with distribution in the ctr and horiz stabilizer tanks differing from the fuel gauges themselves. actual fuel quantity distribution was illegal.
corporate captain reported taking evasive action to avoid a uas on final approach.
engine stopped responding to pilot inputs. pilot shutdown the engine and diverted to an enroute airport.
a320 captain reported experiencing loss of g hydraulic system in cruise flight. flight continued to destination airport and landed safely.
a320 captain reports inadvertent slide deployment by utility crew removing trash from the aft galley.
two a321 flight attendants reported suffering physical effects from noxious fumes in the cabin.
air carrier pilot reported las atc does not allow aircraft to depart from the runway required to comply with climb gradients to avoid terrain due to high outside air temperatures.
b737 pilot reported inflight failure of apu resulted in one source of electrical power. flight diverted and landed safely.
the flight crew departing mdw inadvertently accepted a 'de-icing complete' transmission intended for another aircraft and had to be recalled prior to takeoff to complete the de-icing process.

an air carrier crew on the mount vernon runway 01 visual approach at dca refused a runway 33 landing and during roll out another aircraft landed on runway 33. the captain applied maximum braking to avoid crossing runway 33 as the other aircraft passed in front. no lasho command was issued.

after departing yip a flight instructor and his instrument student were cleared direct to svm; 'cleared for the vor a approach;' as requested. after departing svm; the iaf/faf; on course for the vor a approach to 1d2; canton-plymouth-mettetal airport atc advised of a track deviation. further inquiry determined the clearance had been for the vor-a approach at yip; not the vor-a to 1d2. svm is the iaf for both procedures. the reporter did not recall if the airport name had been appended to either the clearance or his readback.
b737-800 pilot reported hearing a noise during taxi which resulted in replacement of both main gear tires.
air carrier flight crew reported a gpws alert after receiving a descend and maintain clearance.
a flt crew diverted for an unconscious pax. despite medical attention and cpr the pax died.

sf340 flt crew reports gpu fire shortly after engine start which is not signaled to the flt crew by the ground crew observing the start. flight attendant reports the fire and passengers are deplaned on to the ramp.
an air carrier captain reported pets being transported by the carrier are routinely mistreated by ground personnel.
fss specialist reported initially giving the wrong svfr clrnc to inbound acft; later correcting the error.
flight instructor reported a dual ecu failure and a resulting diversion to a nearby airport.

pilot became disoriented during an instrument approach in imc conditions. pilot discovered the track error by noticing his previous error while programming his ipad for the approach. pilot reprogrammed the approach and landed safely in vmc.
distracted by a late change in transition routing; lj31 crew fails to level at 1500 ft msl on the teb dep.
c310 pilot reported the right engine began surging after takeoff making aircraft control difficult. pilot returned to departure airport and landed safely.
b737 flight crew reported receiving a cpdlc that contained a fix for a nearby ils when the fix needed was an enroute waypoint.  the spelling was the same for each location.

b757 flight crew reports discovering during preflight that the 'spd brk auto stow' circuit breaker on the p6 panel is pulled and collared. maintenance is called and it is determined that an mel that was cleared by maintenance over a month ago was not properly accomplished.
air carrier captain reported a flap disagree during climb. flight continued to destination airport and made a zero flap landing.
zse controller described an eram anomaly that caused data block jumping; the reporter suggesting the eram auto acquisition parameters be changed to preclude future occurrences.

b767-300 first officer is informed after the fact that the weight and balance calculations for a flight he flew were incorrect. the error occurred when the operations representative added up the various bin loads and passengers on board incorrectly then provided that incorrect information to the flight crew to preform weight and balance calculations.
general aviation jet captain on standard terminal arrival route proceeded to the initial approach fix before being cleared off the arrival. the aircraft had been given a heading for traffic.
b737-800 air carrier pilot reported an oil pressure bypass malfunction during climb. the aircraft returned to the departure airport and landed.
a flight crew refused to fly a b737-800 after a logbook entry stated 'potable water failed epa testing; needs disinfected' but did not contain a sign off after the required 48 hour compliance period.
an air carrier requested that its pilots fly spiraling descent 'assault' approaches into combat area airports without proper training or reference material.

approach controller reminded a cessna 750 captain of his failure to advise before reducing below 250kts as specified on the wilkes barre 3 star to teb. reporter believes this restriction is not appropriate as the aircraft nears teb.
a319 captain experienced unusual braking behavior during an unexpected electrical switchover. no anomalies were noted and the aircraft was taxied to the gate.

air carrier captain reported the unannounced closure of a tracon that was possibly due to an 'atc zero' event caused a divert for fuel. captain reported there was only one atc controller working multiple positions.
oak tower controller and pilot reported that the pilot did not comply with departure instructions causing them to fly into conflict with traffic inbound on an instrument approach.
air carrier ground personnel reported returning to the gate to secure hazmat.
the primary vacuum sys of a vfr bellanca super viking failed in imc. the alternate vacuum functioned and the plt filed ifr receiving a lower clrnc to vmc.
b767-300 captain reported hazmat was incorrectly loaded; ramp personnel corrected the error.
air taxi flight crew reported atc issued a low altitude alert departing cyxx.
b737 flight crew reported a rejected takeoff due to a 'speed brake do not arm' light.

a line mechanic reports an electric type scissor lift equipment moved up (vertically); uncommanded; while in the drive mode. the uncommanded upward movement caused lower surface damage to the b767-300 right-hand outboard trailing edge flap.

an a320 flight crew declared an emergency and returned to their departure airport for an overweight landing following a left engine over temperature event.  during the return some fms and performance data functions failed to function.
an air carrier pilot reported suspected gps jamming.
general aviation pilot reported loss of aircraft control when they became distracted with a door unlocked indication. pilot recovered aircraft and continued flight.
cle ctlr rpts new automation color scheme for data tags reduces situational awareness and contributed to an ops error.

falcon 50 flight crew reported the autopilot failed to capture the assigned altitude during descent. this failure caused an altitude deviation before the crew could arrest the descent and the resulting terrain alert.
b757 captain reported a flight attendant suffered a minor injury due to an abrupt stop to avoid a fuel truck.
c525 pilot reported a runway excursion on wet runway during the landing rollout.
erj-170 flight crew reported encountering wake turbulence on descent into sdf that resulted in a momentary overspeed.
air carrier flight crew reported loss of gps signal in cruise operations reportedly due to gps jamming exercises.
a320 captain reported lights from a baggage facility and airport construction obstruct the flight crew's vision at night.
an a340-300 was dispatched and returned to the field with a nose gear retraction prob. found nose gear pinned for acft towing and not removed.
cessna 152 student pilot reported misidentifying traffic to follow and created a near mid air collision situation with other traffic in the pattern.
b767 flt crew reports refusing acft fuel leak that maintenance insists is within deferrable limits.
an instructor pilot and his student were momentarily blinded by a green laser while in level flight at 4;500 msl.
b737-700 captain reported that a major fuel spill occurred during re-fueling but flight crew was not notified.
air carrier captain reported poor braking on landing in lex on a snow covered runway that had been reported as 'wet'.
air carrier captain reported a track deviation occurred when the similar fix names omrod and omrad were confused.

a bonanza plt experienced loss of throttle ctl on short final at teb. when he taxied clr of the rwy he failed to hold short of another rwy hold line because of confusing markings and distr due to the throttle prob.
air carrier captain reported temporary gps navigation anomalies during descent.
rptr states that msq ndb at cjr has been decommissioned; while apch plates using this navaid are still in existence.
b777 flight crew reported a loud bang on climbout resulting in a return to the departure airport.
caravan 208 pilot reported striking a barrier that was across a taxiway after being cleared on it. there was no damage to the aircraft and the pilot continued taxi to parking.

all crew members began to feel irritated eyes; nose; throat; nausea and headaches during a climb phase in an dc-9-87 aircraft. flight diverted. the crew was informed that maintenance had recently lubed the jt8d-217c engine bleed valves.
a b747-400 captain reports outdated and/or duplicate charts of different dates are included in the approach chart package provided on board the aircraft.
a commuter jet captain appears to believe that ground crews at jfk fail to communicate effectively during aircraft dispatch.
c182 pilot reported that gusty wind conditions on final resulted in a loss of aircraft control.
b777 flt crew concerned with possible hazmat cargo.
flight crew reported returning to departure airport following a malfunction of the engine bleed air valve.
a b767 pilot reported a near overspeed of the aircraft that he attributed to distraction and a perceived lack of familiarity with a new flight instrument display caused by inadequate training.
a b737-500's number 2 eng stalled on start while attempting to start number one eng that was not rotating and distracting the crew. the number two eng subsequently over-temped.

erj 145 first officer reported wind shear and severe turbulence on final approach due to a thunderstorm; resulting in uncontrolled airspeed and altitude. the flight performed a go around and diverted to an alternate airport.

a b737 pre-departure clearance to dfw included direct debbb jovem2. in flight the route clearance changed to the debbb2 star but since both jovem2 and debbb2 include the debbb waypoint; the crew somehow missed the revision which resulted in vectors for a high; fast arrival.
helicopter encroached on airport airspace without being in contact with unicom frequency. reporter of departing aircraft had near miss with encroaching airplane.
cl600 flt crew encounters wake turb during the novss1 dep from atl.
crj-900 captain reported that; while landing; he heard atc clear an aircraft for takeoff from an intersecting runway before he had rolled through the intersection.

tower controller issued a go around to an aircraft attempting to execute an instrument approach that was unable to remain on course; the reporter noting the pilot should have given more information to atc during this event.

b737-300 flight crew reports being unable to pressurize after takeoff. qrh procedures are complied with but still no pressurization and the flight returns to the departure airport. post flight reveals that the e&e compartment door is open and the door warning system is inoperative.
c172 flight instructor reported the engine failed temporally during a training flight.
medium large transport first officer reported atc advised of a low altitude alert departing vny airport.
air carrier flight crew reported on departure worsening weather and an airborne conflict at myam resulted in a gpws terrain caution.

zma center controller reported radio frequency problems in an area of one of their sectors.  the controller stated they could not talk to an aircraft that was experiencing icing and had to have another aircraft relay instructions for them.
emb-145 captain reported encountering an enhanced ground proximity warning system alert during initial approach to airport.
the first officer of a b737-800 reported that both eec's and both pfd's went into alt mode and airspeed deviation in yellow.
a b737-700 was released for svc after a major alteration accomplished and approved on form 337. airworthiness release was not signed.
flight attendant reported the aircraft cleaners are proceeding onto the aircraft before all passengers are deplaned which does not conform with social distancing.
emb-145 flight crew reported electrical issues and safety concerns after landing and taxiing to the gate.
flight crew reported an incorrect altitude read back and a crm failure; resulted in a low altitude alert.
be55 plt experiences alt dev when alt hold fails to capture while plt is distracted reprogramming avionics for a rwy change.
flight instructor reported a runway excursion occurred during a training flight when the student attempted to take off again after landing.
c172 instructor reports shutting down short of his parking place due to a fuel truck in the way. another company c172 attempting to taxi past strikes the rudder with a wingtip.
air carrier captain reported an unstable approach due to poor crm and lack of flying.
b767 captain reported a leading edge slat asymmetry issue after takeoff. the flight crew performed an air turn back and precautionary landing at departure airport.
b757 flt crew has a cockpit window pressure leak.
e-175 first officer reported a communication breakdown between flight crew and atc resulting in takeoff without clearance.
b737-700 fails to pressurize when flight crew does not note engine bleeds were closed.
a c172 pilot lost situational awareness and flew into class b airspace while distracted by the new efb he was using.
crew of b757 may have taken another flt's clrnc and dsnded to fl330 from fl360 in zma airspace.

a b767 flight crew aborted tkof on a ferry flight after noticing an 'unscheduled stab trim' caution message. crew realized maint had assigned unauthorized mel item to previous stab write-up to release acft.

emb 505 captain reports an emergency landing due to hydraulic failure which results in a blown main tire.  in the aftermath the aircraft log is completely overlooked and no discrepancy is entered.  this oversight is not detected until six days later.
center controller described a lengthy airspace blocking event when information regarding the block and/or strip data was not passed on during the position relief briefing.
after landing at mem a first officer took control of an aircraft and forcefully stopped it because captain was not following taxi instructions and putting the aircraft into a conflict.
a b757 flt crew programmed the wrong sid into the fmc during preflight. the error stemmed from an improper flt number in acars.
b737 flight crew reported a bird strike with about 20 pigeons while on short final to bur.
air carrier pilot reported the need to take evasive action during taxi when a tug drove in front of the aircraft.
an md-82 flight crew reported nose gear light remained red on extension during approach. they ran the procedure; extended the nose gear with the emergency lever; and got a green light.
Crashed into lake while attempting to land. Aircraft porpoised and sank into a lake. Improper level off. Improper recovery from bounced landing.
an md80 crew departing on the ind rocky5 question the ambiguous wording about the initial dep hdg of 227 or 212 degs.
wdb flt crew fails to note a substantive change in assigned sid from vidp because the info was buried in 19 pages of un-annotated notams.
cl600 crj flt crew has a track and hdg dev during apch to mem due to acft equip probs.
air carrier flight crew reported an inadvertent slide deployment of a door during preflight procedures.
a b747-400 failed to receive a revised maintenance release following the deferral of the stab trim indicator which malfunctioned after gate departure but prior to takeoff.
a b757-200 pilot questions intl s american operations without acars operational because of language and hf equipment difficulties.
emb135 capt on the ramp at bos takes evasive action to avoid collision with quick moving acft pushing back.
c501 captain reported a loss of cabin pressure and cabin door seal failure when water in door pressurization bleed lines froze necessitating a rapid descent from cruise altitude.

salt lake tracon controller reported observing a departure on a heading towards conflicting terrain and airspace. reporter stated the local tower retains aircraft on their frequency for extended periods without proper monitoring.

an air carrier captain reported that at the flight's destination ground personnel transferring baggage reported that bags were loaded onto his aircraft and not accounted for on either the electronic weight and balance or the load closeout.
m03 controller voiced concern regarding the new tower departure coordination procedure noting the tower often fails to coordinate when a data tag fails to acquire.
b777 flight attendant reported the jump seat belts on the aircraft are too short and therefore unsafe for many flight attendants.
b757 captain reported a pressurization failure and divert to a nearby airport.
c560 loses right-hand cargo door on tkof.
zab controller reports of an aircraft that was below the terrain and the msaw [minimum safe altitude warning] doesn't alarm.
a319 first officer reported a b737 was vectored in front of their aircraft while on approach to runway 4l at dtw which caused them to take evasive action.
a b737 first officer is advised by atc during descent into iad; that the altimeter setting obtained via digital atis is not correct and that it is a nationwide problem.
an a320 flight crew declared and emergency and diverted to the nearest suitable airport following an advisory of burning electrical odors in the aft galley from a flight attendant.
despite multiple; apparently erroneous; eicas messages and malfunctioning communications radios the flight crew of a cl-300 elected to continue and complete their three hour ifr flight.
be-58 pilot reported the nose gear collapsed causing the propellers to strike the ground during landing.
